title: arXiv Mathematics — 3 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv supplies no official trending chart; this is an inferred ordering of notable work, not a popularity ranking, and the very recent batch offers little citation or independently corroborated attention evidence.

sections.title: Construction of the 2D non-Abelian Yang-Mills-Higgs measure via stochastic quantisation
sections.abstract: The authors construct the two-dimensional non-Abelian Yang-Mills-Higgs measure through a gauge-covariant stochastic-quantisation approximation whose limiting Langevin flow has a unique invariant measure.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove global well-posedness of the stochastic Yang-Mills-Higgs flow on gauge orbits over the two-dimensional torus and construct its unique invariant probability measure; the introduction identifies that measure as the sought-after field-theory construction.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A two-dimensional torus, a connected compact Lie group with an invariant inner product, and a finite-dimensional orthogonal Higgs representation with an invariant symmetric potential operator; non-perturbative for fixed coupling constants.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is specific to dimension two and the stated gauge/Higgs setting; it does not establish global well-posedness or measure construction in three dimensions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors claim a first construction for this non-Abelian model; the result combines global well-posedness, uniform-in-time bounds, and uniqueness of an invariant law, and it is cross-listed across analysis, probability, and mathematical physics. A Warwick probability-seminar talk on 28 October independently discussed the construction before the arXiv submission.

sections.title: A proof of the spectral rigidity for complex projective space
sections.abstract: The authors claim that the spectrum of the Hodge Laplacian in any one fixed degree determines complex projective space, up to holomorphic isometry, among compact connected Kähler manifolds.
sections.claimed_result: For each fixed pair of integers (p,n) with 0 ≤ p ≤ n, equality, including multiplicities, of the degree-p Hodge spectrum with that of Fubini–Study CP^n forces holomorphic isometry; the proof combines spectral, wave-trace, topological, and curvature arguments.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The comparison manifold is compact, connected, Kähler, and without boundary; the hypothesis is exact equality of the full spectrum in one fixed form degree, including multiplicities.
sections.unique_caveat: The result concerns exact full spectra in the Kähler class, not partial spectra, approximate isospectrality, or arbitrary Riemannian manifolds.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It addresses a stated folklore inverse-spectral conjecture and strengthens the scalar-spectrum statement to every fixed degree 0 ≤ p ≤ n; the introduction gives a theorem and proof route covering exceptional Pell-sequence cases.

sections.title: Local scaling limit of the four-dimensional uniform spanning tree
sections.abstract: The author proves that the uniform spanning tree of Z^4, viewed from the origin, converges locally after logarithmically corrected rescalings to a spatial Brownian Kesten tree, with a related super-Brownian occupation-measure limit.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves local rooted spatial Gromov-weak convergence to an infinite Brownian Kesten tree, and convergence of the rescaled space-time occupation measure to infinite canonical super-Brownian motion.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The wired uniform spanning forest on Z^4, rooted at the origin, with intrinsic metric, vertex volume, and spatial labels rescaled by the paper's dimension-specific constants and logarithmic factors.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is for the four-dimensional lattice and this local topology; two scaling constants are not individually known explicitly, although their product is identified.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper supplies a local scaling limit in the critical four-dimensional setting and jointly tracks intrinsic distance, volume, and Euclidean embedding; its introduction places it against previously missing local-limit results and derives sharp first-moment asymptotics.

sections.title: Near-optimal bounds for the critical 2d SHF and the delta-Bose gas
sections.abstract: The authors improve the upper bound on the N-th moment of the critical two-dimensional stochastic heat flow to exp(exp(C N^(1+o(1)))), close to a known lower bound, and give a fixed-N spectral formula for the delta-Bose ground-state energy.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish the exponential scale of the ground-state energy predicted by Rajeev's conjecture up to a vanishing error in the exponent, and derive, for each fixed N, a formula in terms of the bottom of a principal-operator spectrum.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Critical two-dimensional stochastic heat flow and the two-dimensional N-body delta-Bose gas; the spectral formula is stated for each fixed N.
sections.unique_caveat: The result reaches the predicted scale only up to a vanishing error in the exponent; the abstract does not claim a complete resolution of Rajeev's conjecture.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract quantifies an improvement from an N^2 exponent to N^(1+o(1)), compares it with an existing lower bound, and connects the estimate to a prediction for the two-dimensional delta-Bose gas; it is cross-listed across probability, mathematical physics, and functional analysis.

sections.title: The proof of the Harary--Hill conjecture: a detailed exposition and an extension to rotation systems
sections.abstract: The author presents a combinatorial proof of the Harary--Hill crossing-number conjecture and proves a broader weighted lower bound for four-vertex subsystems of every rotation system of K_n.
sections.claimed_result: For every rotation system of K_n, the number of four-vertex subsystems realizable as one-crossing drawings of K_4, plus three times the number of non-realizable subsystems, is at least Z(n), the Harary--Hill lower-bound expression.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Complete graphs K_n for n ≥ 3; the main general statement concerns rotation systems and four-vertex subsystems, rather than drawings themselves.
sections.unique_caveat: The preprint describes itself as an exposition of a short proof uploaded to GitHub in October 2026 while adding a broader combinatorial statement; this summary has not independently checked that proof.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It targets a longstanding extremal-combinatorics conjecture and states a general rotation-system inequality from which the conjectured crossing number follows. A separate October exposition and mathematical commentary discuss the underlying claimed proof; that attention is not evidence of peer review.

sections.title: Improved lower bounds for the kissing number in dimensions 49 to 61
sections.abstract: The author gives explicit kissing configurations in every dimension from 49 through 61, improving the best previously published lower bound in all thirteen dimensions by a total of 506,461 points.
sections.claimed_result: The author reports improved lower bounds in each dimension 49 ≤ d ≤ 61, with margins from 232 to 159,220 points and exact integer verification of the listed configurations.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Euclidean kissing configurations in dimensions 49–61, constructed from a shell of the extremal even unimodular lattice P_48p and lower-dimensional antipodal configurations.
sections.unique_caveat: These are lower bounds, not exact kissing numbers; the computational certificate claim does not establish optimality.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The improvement covers thirteen dimensions and uses a stated combination of lattice-shell lifts, local search, and maximum-coverage optimization; the arXiv record says exact-integer certificates and code/data are provided.

sections.title: Quantitative finiteness for maximal complex totally geodesic submanifolds of non-arithmetic ball quotients
sections.abstract: The authors bound the number of maximal complex totally geodesic submanifolds of a smooth finite-volume non-arithmetic ball quotient linearly in its volume, with a constant depending only on complex dimension.
sections.claimed_result: For a smooth finite-volume non-arithmetic complex ball quotient, the number of maximal complex totally geodesic submanifolds is at most a dimension-dependent constant times the volume.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Smooth finite-volume non-arithmetic ball quotients; the implied constant depends on complex dimension.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not state an explicit value for the dimension-dependent constant, and the theorem's non-arithmetic and smoothness hypotheses delimit its scope.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It upgrades previously published finiteness theorems, as identified by the authors, to a volume-order bound and connects algebraic geometry, differential geometry, and dynamics by cross-listing.

sections.title: Stability of negative-regularity mixing and applications to stochastic fluids
sections.abstract: The authors show that expected contraction of a negative Sobolev norm, expressing mixing of an advected scalar, is stable under perturbations of the joint scalar-velocity process and apply it to three stochastic-fluid settings.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish perturbation stability of negative-regularity mixing and apply it to a hyperviscous Boussinesq-type system, a passively advected scalar for stochastically forced two-dimensional Navier--Stokes, and an implication from such mixing to enhanced dissipation.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Scalars advected by random vector fields; the applications use the specific systems and smooth-in-time stochastic forcing described in the paper.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract's applications are to these stated systems; it does not claim a universal mixing theorem for all stochastic fluid equations.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It supplies an abstract stability result with applications to active and passive scalar equations and enhanced dissipation, and its cross-listing links probability, PDE, and dynamics.
